title: Solara Health: sustained 5xx/429 + retry storm — remediation & settlement discussions
text:
Solara Health: sustained 5xx/429 + retry storm — remediation & settlement discussions

['From: Sara Li <ops@solarahealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <cto@solarahealth.com>, procurement@solarahealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 spike + retry storm impacting checkout

Aditya —

We observed a sustained elevation in 5xx and 429 responses across our checkout and patient-intake endpoints starting ~2026-08-16T23:45Z. The elevated errors and resultant client-side retry loops caused timeouts, doubled request volumes, and a backlog in our worker pool. This directly impacted 8% of checkout attempts in the window; revenue is at risk for today.

Attached is a short log excerpt (request_log_excerpt.csv) showing the error codes and timestamps. We need:
- immediate mitigation plan and ETA to restore normal error rates
- confirmation of root cause analysis timeline
- proposed customer remediation (credits/refund) and a formal SLA remediation offer

Raj (CTO) is on this thread; procurement is copied for billing follow-up. We need an exec-level commitment on credits if you confirm this is on Redwood. Please treat as P1.

Thanks,
Sara Li
Sr. Director, Site Reliability
Solara Health

--
Attachment: request_log_excerpt.csv (10 KB)

Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 spike + retry storm impacting checkout

Aditya / team —

Quick triage update from SRE: we saw a cascading failure triggered by an autoscaler policy change deployed accidentally in the EU region that incorrectly classified long-tail requests as cold and scaled down inference workers while traffic spiked from Solara. Client-side retries (no jitter) amplified traffic and saturated the ingress queue, leading to 429s and downstream 5xx as requests timed out waiting for workers.

Mitigation applied (completed 09:30 PDT):
- Reverted autoscaler policy to previous stable config (rollback complete)
- Temporarily applied conservative rate limit for Solara's IP range to reduce retry amplification
- Forced warm KV cache for affected model family and pre-warmed two additional inference pools in us-west-2
- Enabled a circuit-breaker to shed excess requests and return fast failures to avoid queue pileups

Current status: error rate falling; we estimate 90% of affected requests have recovered; working on full catch-up for delayed requests. We will produce a detailed RCA and timeline in the next 48 hours and share mitigation artifacts.

Attachment: initial-mitigation-timeline.md (internal)

Hannah Schmitt
SRE Manager — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal: remediation credits + next steps (draft)

Sara / Raj / Procurement —

First, thank you for the clear escalation and for working with Hannah’s team on mitigation. From a commercial stance, we want to resolve this quickly and fairly. Below is an initial settlement proposal we can finalize after the RCA:

- One week of service credit (7% of monthly invoice) applied to the August invoice, delivered as a billing credit
- Joint postmortem within 72 hours with technical leads and a committed list of actions for improved autoscaler safety checks
- Priority engineering support for the next 30 days and a dedicated Slack channel for near-term coordination

If acceptable in principle we’ll route a formal agreement to procurement (draft attached: settlement_draft.docx). If you need a different structure (percentage, one-time refund, or SLA addendum), tell us what you'd prefer and we’ll escalate internally.

Marissa Cole

Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 11:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: remediation credits + next steps (draft)

Thanks Marissa. Appreciate the quick mitigation. Procurement is pushing for a larger commercial remediation given the measurable revenue impact and the fact this touched our checkout flow. Our ask (preference order):
1) One-time invoice refund equivalent to 15% of August estimated usage (preferred)
2) If refund not possible, 14 days of service credit applied to next invoice
3) Formal SLA guarantee (service credit schedule) for similar incidents going forward

We also require an executive call (VP Sales + VP SRE) to confirm commercial terms before procurement signs anything. Can you provide a firm commercial response by COB tomorrow? I’ve attached a short impact spreadsheet.

Sara Li
Sr. Director, Site Reliability
Solara Health

Subject: Re: Proposal: remediation credits + next steps (draft) — Redwood offer and next steps

Sara / Raj / procurement team —

Thanks for being direct about expectations. Internal review with Marissa / legal / finance produced the following customer-facing offer:

1) One-time credit equal to 9% of the August invoice applied as a billing credit (reflects measured impact while leaving room to finalize RCA-based adjustments)
2) Complementary 60-day trial of Redwood Dedicated for Solara’s checkout traffic (zero charge) to provide capacity isolation and reduce cross-tenant risk while you evaluate Dedicated
3) Joint postmortem within 48 hours with execs included (VP Sales and SRE will join) and a written RCA delivered within 72 hours
4) We will include an SLA addendum template for your legal/procurement that defines credit triggers and response timelines; we can negotiate terms during the procurement review

If this is acceptable we will issue the billing credit immediately and route the legal draft for signature. We can also arrange the exec call tomorrow morning — please suggest times.
